snapshot.text: Health insurance and budgets are central to policy. Costs are rising as the population ages, so the government is pushing efficiency measures alongside extra spending. A new five-year WHO partnership targets accessible, resilient services, and youth nicotine use is a current focus.

minister.name: Frank Vandenbroucke
minister.role: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Public Health and Social Affairs

priorities.title: WHO country cooperation strategy 2026–2030
priorities.text: Belgium and WHO signed a five-year framework aiming to make health services more accessible, equitable and resilient, with a focus on noncommunicable diseases and mental health.

priorities.title: 2026 health insurance budget and cost control
priorities.text: Federal authorities added about €1.5bn to health insurance spending for 2026, within a 2% growth target, alongside measures to curb medicine waste and cap pharmaceutical costs.

priorities.title: Revised healthcare reform after doctors' objections
priorities.text: The minister revised proposed reforms after doctors' unions objected, including a cap on fee supplements that would start in 2028 only if hospital financing changes.

netherlands.text: Belgium and the Netherlands launched the BeneluxA pharmaceutical initiative in 2015, with three other countries, to share health technology assessments and jointly negotiate medicine prices.
